# Cursor Rules Generator (.mdc)

> The modern, client-side, multi-file rules generator for Cursor AI, Claude Code, and Windsurf.

## Overview
Cursor Rules Generator (https://cursor.pacebowl.com/) is a developer utility designed to generate modular, path-scoped `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files. It prevents AI context bloat and token waste by scoping development instructions to specific file patterns via glob matching.

## Key Capabilities & Tools
- **Live Cursor Glob Matcher & Token Simulator**: Interactive path tester that evaluates active file paths (e.g. `app/checkout/page.tsx`) against rule globs and visualizes token savings in real time (~75% context reduction).
- **Terminal 1-Line Setup**: 1-click clipboard copy of shell script (`mkdir -p .cursor/rules && cat << 'EOF' ...`) for instant command-line file creation without zip downloads.
- **Modular Multi-file Architecture**: Exports rules to `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` with standard YAML frontmatter (`description`, `globs`, `alwaysApply`).
- **1-Click Zip Export**: Packages the full `.cursor/rules/` directory structure using client-side JSZip.
- **Universal Multi-Target Export**: Generates `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` (Cursor), `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code), `.windsurfrules` (Windsurf), and legacy `.cursorrules`.
- **Framework & Library Presets**: Next.js 15 (App Router, Server Actions), React 19, Vue 3 / Nuxt, Python FastAPI (Pydantic v2), Golang, Node.js, Tailwind CSS v4, Shadcn UI / Radix primitives, Vercel AI SDK (streamText/streamUI), Supabase (with RLS), and Zod.
- **Engineering Guardrails**: Anti-AI Hallucination (strict package.json discipline), Strict TypeScript, Early Return pattern, error boundary conventions, and zero redundant AI comments.

## Engineering Guides & Tutorials
- [Cursor Rules (.mdc) vs .cursorrules Migration Guide](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/blog/cursor-rules-mdc-vs-cursorrules.html): Explains the technical rationale behind replacing monolithic .cursorrules with path-scoped .mdc files, glob simulation, and terminal 1-line setup.
- [How to Write Next.js 15 Cursor Rules](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/blog/how-to-write-nextjs-15-cursor-rules.html): Production rules for App Router, React Server Components boundaries, Server Actions validation, and Shadcn/AI SDK integration.

## Dedicated Framework Rules (.mdc)
- [Next.js 15 Rules](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/rules/nextjs-15.html): App Router, Server Actions, and React Server Components boundaries.
- [Python FastAPI Rules](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/rules/python-fastapi.html): Pydantic v2, async endpoints, and dependency injection.
- [React 19 & Vite Rules](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/rules/react-vite.html): Pure functional components, clean custom hooks, and strict TypeScript.
- [Vue 3 & Nuxt Rules](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/rules/vue3-nuxt.html): Composition API with <script setup>, Pinia state actions.
- [Supabase & RLS Rules](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/rules/supabase.html): Row Level Security enforcement and typed client SDK.
- [Tailwind CSS v4 Rules](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/rules/tailwind-css.html): Atomic utility classes, cn() merging, and mobile-first styles.
- [Golang Rules](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/rules/golang.html): Idiomatic error wrapping, context.Context propagation, and struct tags.
- [Cloudflare Workers Rules](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/rules/cloudflare-workers.html): Hono routing, edge D1/KV storage, and serverless constraints.
- [Rules Directory Hub](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/rules/): Complete overview of production-grade Cursor rules.
- [Rules Open API (JSON)](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/api/rules.json): Direct structured JSON catalog of all 8 production rules and raw .mdc contents.
- [Model Context Protocol Specification](https://cursor.pacebowl.com/api/mcp.json): MCP server manifest and client configuration blueprint for IDE agents.

## Modern .mdc vs Legacy .cursorrules
- **Legacy `.cursorrules`**: Single monolithic file injected into every prompt. Leads to high token usage, context contamination, and conflicting instructions.
- **Modern `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`**: Modular files with YAML frontmatter. Loaded conditionally only when matched by the active file's glob pattern (e.g. `app/**`).

## Usage
1. Open https://cursor.pacebowl.com/
2. Select target frontend, backend, database, and styling presets.
3. Configure code quality guardrails (strict types, anti-hallucination, early return).
4. Test your globs in the Live Glob Matcher to preview context token savings.
5. Click "Terminal 1-Line" to paste directly into your IDE terminal, or click "Download .zip".
